title: Counterfeiting coin, Government stamps, currency-notes or bank-notes
old_text: Counterfeiting coins (IPC 231-232), Government stamps (IPC 255), and currency or bank-notes (IPC 489A) were previously dispersed across chapters XII and XVIII with punishments ranging up to life imprisonment.
new_text: Whoever counterfeits, or knowingly performs any part of the process of counterfeiting, any coin, Government stamp, currency-note or bank-note, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Dispersed in IPC 231, 232, 255, 489A with penalties up to life imprisonment or 10 years and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description up to ten years, and fine (BNS Section 178).
explanation: Consolidates multiple fragmented IPC counterfeiting provisions across coins, revenue stamps, and currency notes into a single unified umbrella section with a unified maximum punishment of life imprisonment.

title: Using as genuine, forged or counterfeit coin, Government stamp, currency-notes or bank-notes
old_text: Selling, buying, receiving, or trafficking in counterfeit coins (IPC 239-241), stamps (IPC 258, 260), or fake currency notes (IPC 489B) were punished under separate provisions.
new_text: Whoever sells, buys, receives, or uses as genuine any forged or counterfeit coin, Government stamp, currency-note or bank-note, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.
punishment_old: Dispersed across IPC 239-241, 258, 260, 489B carrying up to life imprisonment and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description up to ten years, and fine (BNS Section 179).
explanation: Consolidates all provisions regarding trafficking, circulation, and commercial deployment of counterfeit coins, stamps, and currency notes into one unified section. Renumbered and merged from IPC Sections 239-241, 258, 260, and 489B.

title: Possession of forged or counterfeit coin, Government stamp, currency-notes or bank-notes
old_text: Possession of counterfeit coin (IPC 242-243), Government stamp (IPC 259), and forged currency notes (IPC 489C) were penalized under separate chapters.
new_text: Whoever has in his possession any forged or counterfeit coin, Government stamp, currency-note or bank-note, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be counterfeit and intending to use it as genuine, shall be punished with imprisonment up to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Dispersed across IPC 242, 243, 259, 489C with penalties up to 7 years or fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to seven years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 180).
explanation: Merges multiple IPC possession offences regarding fake coins, revenue stamps, and forged banknotes into a single section requiring proof of mens rea to circulate or use as genuine.

title: Making or possessing instruments or materials for forging or counterfeiting coin, Government stamp, currency-notes or bank-notes
old_text: Making or possessing machinery, dyes, plates, or paper for counterfeiting coins (IPC 233-235), stamps (IPC 256-257), or notes (IPC 489D) were scattered across chapters XII and XVIII.
new_text: Whoever makes, performs any part of making, buys, sells, or disposes of, or has in his possession, any machinery, instrument, plate, or material for the purpose of being used for counterfeiting coin, stamp, or currency-note, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.
punishment_old: Dispersed across IPC 233-235, 256, 257, 489D up to life imprisonment and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description up to ten years, and fine (BNS Section 181).
explanation: Consolidates all offences relating to the production, possession, or procurement of printing presses, dyes, engraving plates, and specialized paper used for counterfeiting.

title: Making or using documents resembling currency-notes or bank-notes
old_text: Penalized making, issuing or using documents resembling currency-notes or bank-notes with fine up to ₹100.
new_text: Whoever makes, or causes to be made, or uses for any purpose, or delivers to any person, any document purporting to be, or resembling, any currency-note or bank-note, shall be punished with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees.
punishment_new: Fine which may extend to five thousand rupees (BNS Section 182).
explanation: Prohibits commercial advertisements, promotional coupons, or play money deceptively resembling official legal tender notes, increasing the fine limit fiftyfold from ₹100 to ₹5,000. Renumbered from IPC Section 489E.

title: Effacing writing from substance bearing Government stamp, or removing from document a stamp used for it, with intent to cause loss to Government
old_text: Penalized effacing writing from stamped paper or removing stamps with intent to cause revenue loss to the Government with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, fraudulently or with intent to cause loss to the Government, effaces writing from stamped substance, or removes a stamp used for a document with intent to use it again, shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 261).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to three years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 183).
explanation: Protects fiscal revenue by criminalizing the chemical erasure or physical removal of adhesive and judicial stamps from legal documents. Renumbered from IPC Section 261.

title: Using Government stamp known to have been before used
old_text: Penalized fraudulently using a Government stamp known to have been previously used with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, fraudulently or with intent to cause loss to the Government, uses for any purpose a Government stamp which he knows to have been before used, shall be punished with imprisonment up to two years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 262).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 184).
explanation: Penalizes recycling canceled revenue or postage stamps to defraud the exchequer. Renumbered from IPC Section 262.

title: Erasure of mark denoting that stamp has been used
old_text: Penalized erasing or removing cancellation marks from used Government stamps with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, fraudulently or with intent to cause loss to the Government, erases or removes from a Government stamp any mark put upon it to denote that it has been used, shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 263).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to three years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 185).
explanation: Criminalizes bleaching, erasing, or washing postal obliteration marks or cancellation seals from stamps. Renumbered from IPC Section 263.

title: Prohibition of fictitious stamps
old_text: Penalized making, issuing, or possessing fictitious postage stamps with fine up to ₹200.
new_text: Whoever makes or knowingly issues, sells, or uses for any postal purpose any fictitious stamp, or has in possession dies or paper for making fictitious stamps, shall be punished with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees.
punishment_new: Fine which may extend to five thousand rupees (BNS Section 186).
explanation: Prohibits the manufacture, sale, or postal transmission of bogus or fictitious stamps, raising the maximum fine twenty-five-fold from ₹200 to ₹5,000. Renumbered from IPC Section 263A.

title: Person employed in mint causing coin to be of different weight or composition from that fixed by law
old_text: Penalized mint employees intentionally causing coins to be of different weight or composition from that fixed by law with imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
new_text: Whoever, being employed in any mint, does any act, or omits what he is legally bound to do, with the intention of causing any coin issued from that mint to be of a different weight or composition from that fixed by law, shall be punished with imprisonment up to seven years, and fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine (IPC Section 244).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to seven years, and fine (BNS Section 187).
explanation: Punishes corruption and illegal debasement of currency coins by employees within government mints. Merges and renumbers IPC Sections 244 and 245.

title: Unlawfully taking coining instrument from mint
old_text: Penalized unlawfully taking coining tools, dies, or instruments out of any mint with imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
new_text: Whoever, without lawful authority, takes out of any mint any coining tool, die, or instrument, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine (IPC Section 245).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine (BNS Section 188).
explanation: Penalizes the theft or unauthorized removal of official coining dies, stamps, or apparatus from sovereign mints. Marks the final section of Chapter X. Renumbered from IPC Section 245.
